This creature uses the Otherworldly Steed stat block. If you already have a steed from this spell, the steed is replaced by the new one.The steed resembles a Large, rideable animal of your choice, such as a horse, a camel, a dire wolf, or an elk. Whenever you cast the spell, choose the steed’s creature type—Celestial, Fey, or Fiend—which determines certain traits in the stat block.Combat. The steed is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, it shares your Initiative count, and it functions as a controlled mount while you ride it (as defined in the rules on mounted combat). If you have the Incapacitated condition, the steed takes its turn immediately after yours and acts independently, focusing on protecting you.Disappearance of the Steed. author: LVDVg5n3IGEBCWns
content: The Tideheart Trinket A quarter of a heart, turned to crystal: deep water blue, clear and cold, like light coming a long way up through black water. It is the size of two cupped hands, and the chambering and the sheared-off vessels are still there inside the stone like flaws in a gem. It is warm — warmer than the air, which is the wrong thing for something pulled out of a fen — and it beats, slowly, faintly. It does not chip and it does not scratch. It has already been broken.The vision. The Tideheart requires attunement. The first time you hold it, it shows you one thing. A beautiful green woman, glowing white, leaves crowning her head, weeping. She closes her hands over her own chest, and her heart bursts. The pieces scatter into the dark, hardening as they fly. The burst drives the mists back in a great ring, baring a bare green valley next to a beautiful lake. Where she stood, a tree: grey, leafless, asleep. A single faint heartbeat, and it is over.While you carry the Tideheart you have advantage on Strength saving throws.Once between dawns, you can press the shard to your own chest or another's: cold salt water floods the lungs and recedes, and it casts death ward — the shard is the only component needed.It is one chamber of a heart — and a heart has four. You cannot shake the feeling that, whole, it could do so much more. Attunement Required Not Equipped Not Proficient

author: DVSDeA29YhlyJV2g
content: The Tideheart Trinket A quarter of a heart, turned to crystal: deep water blue, clear and cold, like light coming a long way up through black water. It is the size of two cupped hands, and the chambering and the sheared-off vessels are still there inside the stone like flaws in a gem. It is warm — warmer than the air, which is the wrong thing for something pulled out of a fen — and it beats, slowly, faintly. It does not chip and it does not scratch. It has already been broken.The vision. The Tideheart requires attunement. The first time you hold it, it shows you one thing. A beautiful green woman, glowing white, leaves crowning her head, weeping. She closes her hands over her own chest, and her heart bursts. The pieces scatter into the dark, hardening as they fly. The burst drives the mists back in a great ring, baring a bare green valley next to a beautiful lake. Where she stood, a tree: grey, leafless, asleep. A single faint heartbeat, and it is over.While you carry the Tideheart you have advantage on Strength saving throws.Once between dawns, you can press the shard to your own chest or another's: cold salt water floods the lungs and recedes, and it casts death ward — the shard is the only component needed.It is one chamber of a heart — and a heart has four. You cannot shake the feeling that, whole, it could do so much more. Attunement Required Not Equipped Not Proficient
